'''Sir Roy Malcolm Anderson''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|FRS|FMedSci|MAE}}<ref name=frs/> (born 12 April 1947) is a leading international authority on the epidemiology and control of infectious diseases. He is the author, with [[Robert May, Baron May of Oxford|Robert May]], of the most highly cited book in this field, entitled ''[[Infectious Diseases of Humans: Dynamics and Control]]''.<ref name=epmc>{{EuropePMC}}</ref><ref name=off>{{Official URL}}</ref> His early work was on the population ecology of infectious agents before focusing on the epidemiology and control of human infections. His published research includes studies of the major viral, bacterial and parasitic infections of humans, wildlife and livestock.<ref>[http://www.vega.org.uk/video/programme/72 Freeview Video 'The Epidemic of Mad Cow Disease (BSE) in the UK, Roy Anderson — a Royal Institution Discourse by the Vega Science Trust]</ref><ref>[http://www.epsrc.ac.uk/Content/Documents/Biographies/RoyAnderson.htm EPSRC biography]</ref><ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20060712110451/http://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/main.jhtml?xml=/news/2006/06/17/nhonours117.xml Telegraph — Honours for those who 'work and serve at the sharp end']</ref> This has included major studies on [[HIV]], [[SARS]], [[foot and mouth disease]], [[bovine tuberculosis]], [[bovine spongiform encephalopathy]] (BSE), [[influenza A]], [[antibiotic resistant bacteria]], the [[neglected tropical diseases]] and most recently [[COVID-19]]. Anderson is the author of over 650 peer-reviewed scientific articles with an [[h-index]] of 125.<ref name=gs>{{Google scholar id}}</ref>

== Education and early life ==
Anderson was born the son of James Anderson and Betty Watson-Weatherburn.<ref name=whoswho /> He attended Duncombe School, [[Bengeo]] and [[Richard Hale School]]. He was awarded a first-class [[Bachelor of Science]] degree in [[zoology]] at [[Imperial College London]] followed by a [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] degree in [[parasitology]] in 1971.<ref name=phd>{{cite thesis|degree=PhD|publisher=University of London|title=A quantitative ecological study of the helminth parasites of the bream (Abramis brama (L.))|first= Roy Malcolm|last=Anderson|date=1971|id={{EThOS|uk.bl.ethos.363435}}|hdl=	10044/1/16195|oclc=|url=https://spiral.imperial.ac.uk/handle/10044/1/16195|website=imperial.ac.uk}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|title=Population Dynamics of the Cestode Caryophyllaeus laticeps (Pallas, 1781) in the Bream (Abramis brama L.)|first=Roy M.|last=Anderson|author-link=Roy M. Anderson|journal=Journal of Animal Ecology|volume=43|year=1974|pages=305–321|doi=10.2307/3367|issue=2|jstor=3367}}</ref>

== Career and research==
He moved to the Biomathematics Department at the University of Oxford as an [[IBM]] [[research fellow]] working on stochastic models of infectious disease spread under Professor Maurice Bartlett FRS. He was appointed to a Lectureship in Parasitology at King's College London in 1974 before moving back to Imperial as a lecturer in Ecology and then becoming Professor of [[Parasite Ecology]] in 1982. He was head of the Department of Biology from 1984 to 1993.<ref name="ww" /> At Imperial College, he also served as Director of the Wellcome Centre for Parasite Infections from 1989 to 1993.<ref name=epmc/>

In 1993 Anderson moved to the [[University of Oxford]] where he was head of the Zoology department and held the [[Linacre Chair of Zoology]] at [[Merton College, Oxford]] until 2000. During this time he founded and served as Director of the Wellcome Centre for the Epidemiology of Infectious Disease - the first such centre in the UK entirely focused on research into the epidemiology and control of infectious diseases - until he resigned "''following two damning reports on the way that the centre has been managed''", however the director of the [[Wellcome Trust]] noted that there was ''“no question of the scientific credibility of Roy Anderson or the centre. It is doing first class work and our priority is to maintain that.”''.<ref>{{cite journal | author = Loder, N.|title = Director of Wellcome centre resigns over damning report|journal = Nature |volume = 404|pages = 696 |date = 13 April 2000 |doi = 10.1038/35008235 | url=https://www.nature.com/articles/35008235|doi-access = free|url-access = subscription}}</ref> His former doctoral students include  [[Angela McLean (biologist)|Angela Mclean]]<ref name=angela/>.<ref name=mathgene/>

===Chief Scientific Advisor of the Ministry of Defence===
He was [[MoD Chief Scientific Adviser|chief scientific advisor]] to the UK [[Ministry of Defence (United Kingdom)|Ministry of Defence]] from October 2004 to September 2007. After that, he returned to his chair in Infectious Disease Epidemiology at the Department of Infectious Disease Epidemiology at [[Imperial College London]].<ref>[http://www.imperial.ac.uk/rector/biography/ Prof. Anderson's Biography at Imperial College], as of 2 July 2008.</ref>

===Rector of Imperial College===
Anderson was appointed the 14th [[Rector of Imperial College]] on 1 July 2008. In his time as Rector he focused on strengthening the emphasis on teaching as well as world renown research at Imperial, and on securing a new site in the White City, West London, to facilitate the expansion of Imperial's molecular and biomedical research, halls of residence, support for innovation and entrepreneurship and teaching facilities. He also negotiated the first overseas campus venture for Imperial in partnership with Nanyang Technological University in Singapore which led to the creation of the Lee Kong Chian School of Medicine in Singapore designed to train doctors to meet Singapore Healthcare needs. He tendered his resignation in November 2009 stating his wish to return to his primary interest in scientific research on global health issues.

=== Director of the London Centre for Neglected Tropical Disease Research ===
He established the London Centre for Neglected Tropical Diseases (LCNTDR) in 2013. The LCNTDR was launched with the aim of providing focused operational and research support for NTD control. The LCNTDR member institutions house leading NTD experts with a wide range of specialties, making the centre a valuable resource for cross-sectoral research and collaboration. It is a joint initiative between the [[Royal Veterinary College]], Imperial College London, the [[London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine]], and the [[Natural History Museum, London]].

=== Membership of Councils, Boards and Committees (National and International) ===
He has sat on numerous government and international agency committees advising on public health and disease control including the [[World Health Organization]], The [[European Commission]], [[UNAIDS]], and the [[Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation]].

He is currently{{when|date=February 2023}} a Vice-President of Fauna Flora International, Chairman of Oriole Global Health Limited, Director of the London Centre for Neglected Tropical Disease Research, Trustee of the Banga Trust and a Trustee of the [[London Institute for Mathematical Sciences]].

He was a [[non-executive director]] of [[GlaxoSmithKline]] 2008–2018, a member of the International Advisory Board of Hakluyt and Company Ltd. 2008–2019, and Chairman of the International Advisory Board of PTTGC Company Thailand, 2014–2018.{{fact|date=February 2023}}

== Controversies ==

Anderson resigned from the [[University of Oxford]] after admitting that he had falsely alleged that a colleague, [[Sunetra Gupta]], had won a position by having an affair with her head of department.<ref>{{cite web | title = ‘I’ve had emails calling me evil’... Meet the Covid scientists at war | url = https://www.standard.co.uk/news/health/coronavirus-scientists-at-war-a4569551.html | year = 2020 | first1 = Samuel | last1 = Fishwick}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | url=https://www.nature.com/articles/35016213 | doi=10.1038/35016213 | title=Oxford epidemiologist wins apology for promotion slur | year=2000 | last1=Loder | first1=Natasha | journal=Nature | volume=405 | issue=6789 | page=872 | pmid=10879499 | s2cid=4304810 | doi-access=free | url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | url=https://www.nature.com/articles/35000388 | title = Top UK epidemiologist suspended after complaints | journal = Nature | volume = 403 | issue = 353 | year = 2000 | doi = 10.1038/35000388 | last1=Loder | first1=Natasha| doi-access = free | url-access = subscription }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | title = Oxford scientist suspended | first1 = John | last1 = Ezard | year = 2000 | url = https://www.theguardian.com/uk/2000/jan/27/johnezard | publisher = [[The Guardian]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | title = Imperial vs Oxford: Covid-19 rivalry may have roots in a sex smear two decades ago | url = https://www.medicalbrief.co.za/imperial-vs-oxford-covid-19-rivalry-may-have-roots-in-a-sex-smear-two-decades-ago/ | year = 2020 }}</ref>
<ref>{{cite web| url = https://archive.today/20200404084131/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/2020/04/04/science-clash-imperial-vs-oxford-sex-smear-created-rival-covid/ | title = Science clash: Imperial vs Oxford, and the sex smear that created rival Covid-19 studies –Rivalry began two decades ago when leading lights of Imperial College and Oxford University worked together | first1 = Daniel | last1 = Foggo | first2 = Katherine | last2 = Rushton | first3 = Sophie | last3 = Barnes | year = 2020}}
</ref> He also resigned from the [[Wellcome Trust]].<ref>{{cite web | title = Charity trustee resigns in probe | url = https://www.oxfordmail.co.uk/news/6633666.charity-trustee-resigns-probe/ | publisher = Oxford Mail }}</ref>
<ref>{{cite journal | url=https://www.nature.com/articles/35000724 | doi=10.1038/35000724 | title=Anderson steps down from Wellcome over Oxford row | year=2000 | last1=Loder | first1=Natasha | journal=Nature | volume=403 | issue=472| doi-access=free | url-access=subscription }}</ref> Gupta demanded a public apology 
<ref>{{cite web | title = Wronged zoologist demands public apology | url = https://archive.today/20231218193327/https://www.timeshighereducation.com/news/wronged-zoologist-demands-public-apology/150731.article | year = 2000 | publisher = Times Higher Education}}</ref> which Anderson later gave.<ref>
{{cite web | title = Anderson apologises | url = https://archive.today/20231218192804/https://www.timeshighereducation.com/news/anderson-apologises/152206.article | year = 2000 | publisher = Times Higher Education}}</ref> Anderson moved, along with many of his staff, to [[Imperial College London]].<ref>{{cite web | title = The Londoner: History behind Imperial and Oxford scientists rivalry | year = 2020 | url = https://www.standard.co.uk/news/londoners-diary/the-londoner-history-behind-imperial-and-oxford-scientists-rivalry-a4403876.html}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Anderson married Janet Meyrick in April 2014 and has three step-children.<ref name=whoswho/>

He enjoys walking, travel to remote destinations, natural history, conservation and wildlife photography.<ref name=whoswho />
